headline: Molecular models predict cancer survival, drug response and immunotherapy toxicity
label: Cancer Outcome And Drug Response
summary: New tools span methylation-based pediatric brain tumor prognostics, cell-line-to-tumour drug response transfer and scRNA-seq prediction of immune toxicity.
synthesis: The dominant thread is predicting clinical oncology endpoints from molecular profiles. These endpoints are survival, therapy benefit, drug response and immunotherapy outcomes. MANTIS trains a neural network on genome-wide DNA methylation from 2,786 children with brain tumors to estimate time-dependent survival and treatment effects. DeSCENT augments bulk RNA-seq with deconvolved, reference-informed cellular profiles for TCGA survival models. For drug response, MODAE+ uses multi-objective domain adaptation with survival and lineage objectives to transfer cell-line pharmacogenomics to TCGA tumours. MulDR preserves omics-specific cell-line relations, and MTDKF fuses metapath topology with domain knowledge to predict miRNA-drug-disease resistance and sensitivity triplets. A biology-informed strand addresses immunotherapy. irAEGIS predicts immune-related adverse event risk from pre-treatment scRNA-seq with a pathway-guided hierarchical model, outperforming seven comparators. Genialis reports that inferring tumor immune state predicts immunotherapy response comparably to outcome-trained signatures. Together, these suggest mechanistic priors can match supervised endpoint fitting.
